name: Turbopack Lightning CSS transform mangling
observations: Project: LaTribu (Next.js + Turbopack dev, Tailwind v4, opennextjs-cloudflare for prod). Discovered while moving the message-details dialog close button to the viewport corner in components/tribe-round/tribe-round/styles.module.scss (composerDialog--messageDetails).

To free a position:fixed child, every transform-family property on the ancestor must compute to none (transform, translate, etc.); any non-none value re-establishes a containing block and its overflow:hidden clips the fixed child.
Lightning CSS (Turbopack) DROPS `translate: none` as a redundant initial value — it disappears from the compiled rule, so Tailwind's `translate: -50% -50%` utility keeps winning.

Lightning CSS NORMALIZES `transform: none` into `transform: translate3d(0px, 0px, 0px)`, which is NOT equivalent to none and re-creates the containing block. So declaring transform:none is counter-productive here.

Cascade-layer placement differs dev vs prod: in the production (opennextjs-cloudflare) build CSS-module classes are emitted UNLAYERED (win over Tailwind @layer utilities); in Turbopack dev the module rule lands in a layer that LOSES to utilities, so even higher-specificity module selectors lose to plain Tailwind utilities for properties like translate.
Reliable override regardless of layer: use !important. An !important author declaration always beats a normal Tailwind utility in any cascade layer.

Workaround to keep `translate: none` from being stripped: route it through an undefined custom property with a none fallback, e.g. `translate: var(--some-unset-var, none) !important;`. The minifier cannot prove it equals the initial value, so it survives and resolves to none at runtime.
Do NOT declare `transform` at all — leave it unset so it stays none. Declaring transform:none triggers the translate3d(0,0,0) rewrite.

When replacing Tailwind animate-in/animate-out with a custom `animation` shorthand, animation-fill-mode resets to none; add `both` (or forwards) or the exit animation snaps back to its base frame (e.g. opacity:1) before Radix unmounts, causing a flicker on close.

Verification caveat: injected <style> blocks (DevTools / document.head.appendChild) BYPASS the build pipeline, so injection tests pass even when the real compiled build fails. Verify fixes against the actual compiled CSS in DevTools or the running build.
A background browser tab throttles requestAnimationFrame, making frame-by-frame animation measurements unreliable there.

name: User memory preference
observations: When the user asks to save something important to memory, they always mean the memory MCP (mcp__memory__*), not file-based memory or any other mechanism.
If the memory MCP is not configured or unavailable, do NOT silently fall back to another mechanism — report it explicitly to the user.
Stated by the user on 2026-06-02 in the LaTribu project.
File-based memory is fully retired and must not be used or recreated; the memory MCP is the single source of truth for all memory.

name: Memory sync to system-config
observations: Every time the memory MCP is modified (any create/update/delete of entities, relations, or observations that changes configs/.mcp-memory/memory.json), commit and push it from the system-config repository to keep memory.json synced across machines.

The system-config repo always lives at $HOME/system-config (the user's home root), OS-agnostic: on Unix/macOS it is $HOME/system-config, on Windows/PowerShell it is $env:USERPROFILE\system-config or $HOME\system-config. Resolve the current environment's home instead of assuming a fixed path.
When committing, stage ONLY the memory.json change (configs/.mcp-memory/memory.json) — do not drag along other unrelated pending changes in system-config (e.g. configs/.codex/config.toml).
Generate the commit message using the /generate-commit-messages skill, then commit and git push to the current branch.
If the push fails (no network, credentials, or remote), report the concrete blocker explicitly and leave the commit made locally.
Stated by the user on 2026-06-02 in the LaTribu project. Relates to 'User memory preference'.

name: Tailwind v4 translate property containing block
observations: Project: LaTribu (Next.js, Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui). Discovered while moving the message-details dialog close button to the viewport corner so it anchors to the screen instead of the dialog box.

The shadcn DialogContent (components/ui/dialog.tsx) centers with the utilities top-1/2 left-1/2 -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2. In this project's Tailwind v4 setup, -translate-x-1/2 compiles to the standalone CSS `translate` property (computed translate: -50% -50%), NOT `transform`.
An element with a non-none `translate` (or transform/filter/will-change) becomes the containing block for position:fixed descendants, AND its overflow:hidden then clips them.

transform: none alone is NOT enough to free a fixed child — you must also set translate: none. Verified live: with only transform:none the computed translate stayed -50% -50% and the fixed child kept positioning relative to the dialog box.

Working recipe (message-details modal close button in components/tribe-round/tribe-round/styles.module.scss): on the dialog content set `inset: 0; margin: auto; height: fit-content; transform: none; translate: none;` to center without a transform/translate, then on [data-slot="dialog-close"] set `position: fixed; top: 1rem; right: 1rem;` to pin it to the screen corner while keeping it inside the focus trap.

Enter/exit animations (animate-in/animate-out) apply their own transform while running and override inline/stylesheet values during the animation, so DOM measurements taken mid-animation are misleading.

name: iOS WebKit fullscreen modal scroll/backdrop pitfall
observations: Symptom: en iOS Safari el modal fullscreen de mobile (ej. detalle de mensaje del feed en components/tribe-round/tribe-round) dejaba scrollear la pagina de fondo, no mostraba blur y parecia 'salirse' de la pantalla.

Causa 1 (scroll del fondo): Radix bloquea el scroll del body, pero en WebKit el scroll chaining / rubber-band del contenedor interno del modal se propaga a la pagina detras al llegar al borde. Fix: agregar overscroll-behavior: contain al unico contenedor scrolleable del modal (ej. __messageDetailsBody) y al overlay. Se acota al modal en vez de poner overscroll-behavior: none global en body/html para no romper pull-to-refresh.

Causa 2 (sin blur): backdrop-filter tenia un typo 'blur(5x)' (valor invalido => navegador descarta toda la declaracion) y faltaba el prefijo -webkit-backdrop-filter que iOS sigue requiriendo. Fix: usar blur(5px) y declarar -webkit-backdrop-filter ademas de backdrop-filter.

Regla general: en cualquier propiedad backdrop-filter para producto, declarar siempre -webkit-backdrop-filter con un valor valido (cuidado con unidades, blur usa px). En overlays/modales fullscreen de mobile, usar overscroll-behavior: contain en el scroll container para que el fondo no scrollee en iOS.
Mantener 100dvh para overlays fullscreen de mobile (no svh) segun docs/conventions/viewport-units.htm; eso estaba bien y no se toca.

Limitacion de validacion: iOS WebKit no se puede ejercitar en el entorno Windows (sin device/simulador); estos fixes son la solucion estandar pero requieren verificacion en iPhone real. Si el fondo aun scrollea tocando areas no-scrolleables del modal, el siguiente paso es un body lock por JS al abrir el modal.
